answer: Burn one fixed-supply token per vote on inspections of canyon erosion, karst sinkholes or tide flooding. Ledger validators check finalized burn receipts and burner signatures; replays count once. Two conflicting burner-signed choices for one receipt void its vote before tally; the token stays destroyed. A 100-token budget buys at most 100 votes across 1, 10 or 100 keys, even with parallel farms or colluders. Extra keys get no free votes. A coalition buying over half the votes controls priorities; a corrupt validator quorum can count unbacked votes. This does not prove unique humans.
